title: Tenant-tailored preflight loader and KV seed controller for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce cold-start frequency and tail latency for Dedicated tenants while preserving predictable throughput guarantees and reasonable memory/cost profiles.

Background: Dedicated fleet customers have strict SLOs for 95/99 latency and contractual throughput commitments. Large language models introduce long weight load times and KV cache coldness that drive first-request latency and early-throughput degradation. Current warm pool mechanisms load full model weights eagerly for a small set of tenants; however this is expensive at scale and does not address KV prefix coverage.

This ticket proposes a tenant-tailored 'preflight loader' which combines a lightweight weight staging approach with an adaptive KV 'seed controller' that primes hot prefixes based on tenant access patterns. The loader supports three modes: eager-full (full weight residency), staged-weight (partial shard residency + weight streaming), and lazy-with-prefetch (delay weight residency but prefetch KV prefixes for anticipated prompts).

Key components:
- Preflight loader: admission controller that decides mode per tenant based on SLA tier, recent QPS, and throughput commitments.
- Staged weight protocol: staged residency of model shards with an LRU residency window and a background streamer to finish weight load during low-latency windows.
- KV seed controller: per-tenant small representative prefix set maintained by sampling production prompts and synthetic prompt generators. The controller exposes a 'seed bundle' that can be applied to new nodes during warm pool handoff or on instance create.
- Admission and placement hooks: integrate with autoscaler to ensure capacity for guaranteed throughput during tenant burst windows; fallback policies when warm capacity is exceeded.

Trade-offs considered:
- Eager full residency reduces first-request tail latency but multiplies GPU memory usage and cost; we avoid making this default except for P0 enterprise tenants.
- Staged residency reduces peak memory but increases bandwidth between streaming and on-demand shards; requires careful admission window sizing.
- Aggressive KV seeding reduces first-token latency for chatty tenants but risks seeding stale/unnecessary kv entries for very diverse prompt distributions.

Success criteria (high-level):
- 95th percentile first-request generation latency reduced by >=30% for tenants on staged-weight mode compared to baseline.
- Cold-start cost (GPU-seconds paid to bring a node to steady-state) reduced by >=20% for seeded tenants.
- No regression in sustained throughput for other tenants on the same fleet beyond 5%.

Security/Privacy: KV seed controller must respect tenant data policies; seeding must not leak PII across tenants. Seed bundles are scoped and encrypted at rest.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (Confluence link below).
- Prototype implementation of preflight loader and KV seed controller in the runtime controller.
- Benchmarks: microbench for weight streaming, end-to-end tenant replay against a staging fleet.
- Migration guide and defaults for Dedicated console controls.

acceptance_criteria: Feature flag deployable to staging without runtime restarts
Per-tenant mode selection applied within 500ms of admission decision
Seed bundle application completes within node initialization window (<= 30s)
Measured improvements meet success criteria for at least 3 test tenants
Console exposes tenant mode and a manual preheat action
metrics: Target 95p first-request latency for staged-weight tenants: <=1.25s
Cold-start GPU-seconds: baseline 120s per node -> target <=96s
Seed-hit ratio goal: >=65% for chatty tenants
Admission rejection rate target: <0.5% during steady-state
notes: Consider adding a small 'hot fingerprint' service that stores tenant-specific KV fingerprints to reduce seed bundle size.
If network egress becomes dominant during staged streaming, switch to a peer-to-peer shard relay inside the rack to reduce cross-host bandwidth.
We should limit eager-full mode to contractual enterprise tiers only; otherwise default to staged-weight for committed tenants and lazy-with-prefetch for low-tier tenants.
